Arg-max over all 25,730 segments: neutral 17,149 / positive 8,148 / negative 433. In the 19,456 segments used by the recipe (6,274 without speech removed): neutral 10,960 / positive 8,080 / negative 416. The median confidence (max probability) of negative arg-maxes is 0.492, a weak decision. positive is frequent in agents' greetings and closings, and some negative examples are lexically neutral (`i need to check my account balance`). Crowd workers were assigned the role of a bank customer or agent and talked by phone following a goal and a rough script (role-play, no emotion instruction). Sentiment polarity (negative / neutral / positive) is an automatic estimate by the Gridspace Speech API, not a human annotation. Moved from the emotion_categories set on 2026-11-04 because the labels are polarity, not emotion [arxiv_s_2010_13929].

Possible label errors: the 3 clips `S95_BIL_CO14_G3` in the neutral folder (`d01_v1`, `d01_v2`, `d03_v1`; speaker SPKM03) sounded angry to the maintainer (2026-10-20), and their median F0 (176-179 Hz) is closer to that speaker's angry (192-229 Hz) than neutral (133-139 Hz) (their loudness is lower, not matching angry). With no documentation this cannot be settled, so the label stays neutral as distributed (maintainer's decision). Only part was listened to, so other errors may exist. Only a third-party survey (KuralHub) calls it acted; the Kaggle description is empty. Nothing documents how labels were made.
